# Third-party license review

Reviewed on 2026-11-13 for the versions recorded in [manifest.json](manifest.json).
This review covers this repository's redistributed code and the library tarball.
It is a record of technical license checks, not a guarantee about every possible
downstream application, document, patent or trademark use.

The project's original code remains MIT licensed. Third-party materials retain
their own terms. Full texts are tracked in [licenses/](licenses/) so they accompany
the source archive, including the StPageFlip patch. The build copies the same texts
to `dist/licenses/`. The human-readable inventory is
[THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md](../packages/vue-flipbook/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md).

## Evidence and scope

- The package bundles pdfjs-dist 5.7.284 and patched page-flip 2.0.7. Vue is external.
- Reviewed all 186 support assets matched by `src/pdf/embeddedAssets.ts`: Adobe CMaps,
  Foxit/Liberation fonts and the OpenJPEG, JBIG2, QCMS and QuickJS WASM files. Their
  filenames and associated license texts are recorded in the manifest.
- Upstream LICENSE/NOTICE files are preserved byte for byte, including the complete
  multi-license JBIG2 notice. The PDF.js build header is also preserved separately.
  The manifest links to the exact npm distribution archive for pdfjs-dist (its
  GitHub distribution repository has no v5.7.284 tag); `source` identifies the file
  within the package, and `section` identifies the extracted build-header notice.
- For QuickJS, use Mozilla's two verbatim remedial license files in
  [commit a3beacc](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/commit/a3beacc1a35f2d285f0505c5489d8cb4a9ebcc89).
  The [v5.7.284 QuickJS README](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/v5.7.284/external/quickjs/README.md)
  identifies both QuickJS and pdf.js.quickjs as MIT. Do not assume the enclosing
  pdfjs-dist package's Apache declaration covers the sandbox.
- PDF.js's prebuilt files contain webpack runtime code. Its
  [v5.7.284 lockfile](https://github.com/mozilla/pdf.js/blob/v5.7.284/package-lock.json)
  pins webpack 5.106.2. The corresponding MIT text is included. The modern build
  used here does not contain the core-js polyfills of the unused legacy build.
- Include Vite's core MIT text (the exact core-license section) and Rolldown's MIT
  text and upstream Rollup/esbuild attributions for emitted runtime helpers.
  This does not claim all build-tool dependencies are shipped to library users.
- Samples are generated by `scripts/create-fixtures.mjs` from original drawings and
  text using PDF standard font references. pdf-lib is a development dependency; its
  implementation and font programs are not embedded in these generated PDFs.
- ICC profiles, alternate legacy PDF.js builds, source maps, Node canvas binaries,
  and PDF.js's external non-WASM codec fallback files are outside the packaged inputs.
  Adding any of them requires another review. Deployment of the demo applications
  requires preserving the additional notices for their own bundled dependencies.

## Keeping the inventory current

`pnpm build` generates Vite's module-level license report and runs
`scripts/package-notices.mjs`. It fails when reviewed versions, support filenames,
upstream notice files, text hashes, or bundled npm dependencies no longer match.
Do not automatically refresh the manifest to make such failures disappear. Inspect
new inputs and their terms, then deliberately update the inventory and notices.

`pnpm test:licenses` checks that missing/altered notices and unreviewed bundled
dependencies are rejected. `pnpm test:package` also compares the exact license bytes
inside both independent consumers installed from the real tarball. This checks the
published-file selection rather than trusting files left in the workspace.

When changing the asset glob or the build pipeline, review the input scope as well
as the manifest. These checks flag inventory drift; they are not a general-purpose
legal scanner and cannot classify arbitrary newly introduced code automatically.

## Downstream distribution

Keep `THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` and applicable `dist/licenses/` texts with redistributed
code/assets. For a browser deployment, carry those notices into the deployed app,
along with notices for Vue and other application dependencies. Do not assume an
app bundler copies files from dependency packages automatically. OFL font terms
continue to apply to the font files; documents and the original application code
do not become OFL merely by using those fonts.
